title: Refuse to feed the mouth with slander’s filth
summary: The shabad uses startling images for corrupt speech: greed as a dog, falsehood as filth, slander as another person’s dirt placed in your own mouth. The mouth is protected by refusing that meal.
takeaway: Refuse to feed the mouth with slander’s filth.
lifeApplication: When a story about someone else would make you feel powerful for a moment, stop at the mouth and refuse to eat what will dirty you.

source.shortMeaning: Greed, falsehood, cheating, and slander are pictured as filth that degrades the mouth and heart.
source.lifeApplication: When slander rises, see it as dirt entering your own mouth and stop before taking it in.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad makes slander bodily and vivid: the harm is not abstract, because the speaker’s own mouth is polluted.
evidence.turn: Treat slander as something the soul consumes, not merely something the tongue releases.
evidence.practicalImplication: When a story about someone else would make you feel powerful for a moment, stop at the mouth and refuse to eat what will dirty you.
